question: Is there a law that makes one birth at a time, in which each knot reads only a bounded holder-step distance and only what is built, that builds in every order what the complete rounds build: for laws with a ration fixed at birth, for the ring that returns (which needs waiting), and for ordinary growth?
inputs: The starts, laws, cutoffs and kinds of order named in the pre-registration; this epic's definitions and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the earlier study's engine (its ticket A), unchanged, as the reference.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration discloses; any change to the reference engine.
primary_observable: For every start, law, cutoff and kind of order: whether each order matches the complete rounds through the cutoff, mismatches or underbuilds; the least number of births to a mismatch; for the family T(d), the least d with no mismatch; every firing of the closing bit; whether any roster read has a group of three or more.
comparators_or_controls: The complete rounds of the earlier study's engine as the reference; the record's birth-by-birth law (R0) and the record's depth guard with the originals supplied (the control); the gate of the new engine's own rounds against the reference, structure by structure.
resource_budget: Each search under ten minutes and 8 GB on one process; anything longer through the shared runner with a row in the long-running index. Breadth-first searches are capped at ten million keys for the rows of the first table and one million elsewhere.
first_executable_signal: The gate (item 1 of the runs); then every order on D2(4,3) under (RATION-3, CANCEL-WAIT) through round 1.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' clause; checks and open items are reported as such.
stop_rule: The study stops when every registered run is done and every prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of laws written by hand on starts built by hand, each to a stated round only. A pass shows that the global scheduler can be removed given a written birth record, spending in a single act and death as the signal of completion. It does not show that the round is dispensable, that holders alone suffice, or that reading is bounded under repeated waits, and it says nothing for HOLD, FILLERS or CAP-3, for starts where a knot that acts meets a knot that waits, or past the round cutoff. No claim about time in physics.
